system_description.narrative_title: Great‑Power Competition amid Energy, Financial and Climate Shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, interdependent system in flux, driven by overlapping great‑power rivalry, regional wars and proxy escalation, volatile energy markets, and stressed financial markets. Transactional deals between major powers, asymmetric attacks by non‑state actors, and ad‑hoc trade accommodations coexist with weakening multilateral norms, producing feedback loops (energy → prices → politics → markets) that reconfigure alignments and policy choices. Extreme weather and supply‑chain shocks amplify economic and security stresses, increasing the probability of spillovers across regions and domains.
system_description.scope: Nation‑states and their alliances, major non‑state armed actors and proxies, global energy and commodity markets, international financial and bond markets, trade and industrial supply chains, multilateral institutions and legal bodies, and climate/extreme‑weather processes that interact across economic, security, technological and informational domains.
system_description.super_system: The global international political‑economic system (the earthwide security, economic and governance order)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine (backed by NATO and Western partners) remain locked in an intensifying conflict with sustained strikes, shifting frontlines and diplomatic deadlock that are reshaping European security.

variables.name: US–China strategic contest
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting economic and strategic primacy through trade and technology barriers, gray‑zone maritime pressure around Taiwan and diplomatic outreach to third parties, forcing allies and markets to recalibrate ties.

variables.name: Gulf maritime and aviation flashpoint
variables.description: Iran and its regional proxies, notably Houthi forces, are mounting attacks on shipping and civilian aviation in the Gulf and Arabian Peninsula, creating acute escalation risks for Gulf states, international carriers and external military actors.

variables.name: Global energy market fragmentation
variables.description: Global fuel markets are being reshaped by state-to-state supply deals, sanctions circumvention, extreme-weather production shocks and producers' strategic choices, accelerating fragmentation and realignment of energy supply chains and market governance.

variables.name: Financial markets and sovereign yield stress
variables.description: Rising sovereign bond yields, stressed European debt markets, leveraged fund vulnerabilities and questions about central‑bank credibility are reallocating financial risk across the US and Europe and constraining monetary and fiscal policy space.
